title: A snapshot or a live view, and neither writable

blocks.text: Immutable collections sidestep the fail-fast and fail-safe choice: nothing can change them, so there is nothing to detect. The page warns that the two ways to hand one out are not alike:
`Roster` keeps its names in a private `ArrayList`, and `add` is written. Write:

items: `snapshot()`: the names as they are now. **A snapshot keeps its contents**: names added later do not appear in it;
`liveView()`: a read-only window on the names. **A live view follows the roster**: names added later appear in it;
**neither can be changed by its holder**: every change on either, `add`, `remove` by index or by value, `set` or `clear`, throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, and the roster itself is unchanged.

cases.says: With ada and bo added, the snapshot and the view both read [ada, bo].
A snapshot taken before bo is added still reads [ada].
A view taken before bo is added reads [ada, bo] afterwards.
add, remove and clear on the snapshot or the view throw UnsupportedOperationException.

concepts: Immutable and unmodifiable collections throw UnsupportedOperationException on any change: they prevent modification instead of detecting it during iteration.
Collections.unmodifiableList is a view that follows its backing list, while List.copyOf is an independent snapshot.
